title: A Signal for the Protocol Revisited
premise: Wren Eastwick navigates the freighter Vesperine along the war's forgotten edges, tending a beacon whose original commission records were erased — and guarding the hold full of memory-backups of the crew's dead, including their own. When the research vessel Calloway's Ghost returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember the future, Wren learns the beacon is a receiver for a peace protocol both warring factions will kill to suppress. Pursued by the navy that once employed them and the separatists who built the backups, Wren must choose between broadcasting the message — which requires waking the backups, including their own younger self, and risking identity collapse — or staying invisible forever. In the end Wren merges with their backup long enough to transmit the protocol, ending the war at the cost of becoming someone new: neither the person who loved nor the one who remembered, but a third self carrying both forward.
about_author: Lior Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics instructor who now writes from a coastal town where the fog often arrives before the weather reports do. Their fiction explores what survives of a person when every part of them can be copied, paused, or overwritten.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishing the Vesperine's quiet route, the maintenance ritual on the unregistered beacon, and the hold of sleeping backups Wren visits nightly, speaking to their own copy without admitting why. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Calloway's Ghost drifts into range, crew de-aged but carrying precise memories of events that haven't happened — including Wren's death. A child-captain named Ivo recognizes the beacon and begs Wren not to touch it. Emotional beat: dread blooming inside wonder.

chapters.title: Duty Is a Kind of Amnesia
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback-structure through the child's borrowed memories: the deep-space expedition found the Protocol, a first-contact handshake that ends wars by forcing mutual memory exchange. The navy ordered it destroyed; the crew refused and paid in years. Emotional beat: love against duty, inherited.

chapters.title: The Hold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Navy interdiction forces the Vesperine to hide inside a debris field while Wren descends into the backup hold and finally admits the copies are people, not cargo. First direct conversation with their own backup. Emotional beat: grief turning into responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Separatists Kept
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Wren and separatist engineer Sefa Anouk). Sefa's salvage ship intercepts them; she reveals she built the backups as insurance for the Protocol and needs the beacon — which is the transmitter — to finish her dead partner's work. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: distrust softening into shared purpose.

chapters.title: Aged Backward, Running Forward
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The de-aged crew begins losing their future-memories as they physically grow toward the present, erasing the map to the Protocol's coordinates. Race against biological time; Ivo dictates everything he still remembers to Wren. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened by tenderness.

chapters.title: The Navy Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Admiral Corvane boards under parley flag, offering Wren reinstatement, restored records, and a life with no hold full of ghosts — if they surrender the beacon. Wren nearly accepts. Emotional beat: temptation of a clean, forgettable life.

chapters.title: Two of Me
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered by Corvane's blockade, Wren wakes their own backup to merge memories and recover the transmission keys only the original commissioning navigator knew. The two selves argue about who gets to survive. Emotional beat: identity as negotiation, not possession.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POV across Wren, Sefa, and Ivo. The merged Wren transmits the Protocol through the beacon during the naval assault; mutual memory floods both fleets, soldiers suddenly holding each other's dead in their heads. Corvane fires anyway — and her own crew refuses the order. Emotional beat: terrible, involuntary empathy as weapon and cure.

chapters.title: Someone New, Carrying Both
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, weeks later. Ceasefire holds; the de-aged crew grows into ordinary futures; Sefa archives the backups openly. The new Wren tends the beacon one last time, then lets it go dark — its work done — and chooses, for the first time freely, whom to be next. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
